purpose: Worldwide source-link registry derived from the global multilingual discovery work in PR #541 plus Quran-specific source/API work in PR #558.
rules: URL is a discovery/source endpoint, not proof of item-level rights.
API availability is not redistribution permission.
Institutional or repository status does not automatically authorize public PDF redistribution.
Item-level license/terms must be captured before public release.
No source in this registry is treated as an AI translation source.

sources.name: Digital Scriptorium
sources.notes: Cross-institutional premodern manuscript discovery across North American member institutions; not a blanket redistribution license.

sources.name: Digital Scriptorium Catalog
sources.notes: Search portal for manuscript records aggregated from member institutions; item-level rights remain separate.

sources.name: Digital Bodleian
sources.notes: Bodleian digital collections; public availability of images does not by itself establish redistribution rights for every item.

sources.name: Yale Arabic and Middle Eastern Electronic Library (AMEEL)
sources.notes: Yale describes approximately 350,000 pages of searchable full text, including Arabic, plus historical manuscript catalogues; access/rights vary during migration.

sources.name: NYPL Arabic Manuscripts Digital Collection
sources.notes: Collection includes Arabic manuscripts from the 7th to late 19th century, including Qur'an items, religious works, law and history.

sources.name: NYPL Archives & Manuscripts — Arabic manuscripts collection
sources.notes: Finding aid for MssCol 116; portions are digitized and the collection has 517 listed image assets.

sources.name: University of Michigan Islamic Manuscripts
sources.notes: More than 1,100 volumes and about 1,800 texts, primarily Arabic, Persian and Ottoman Turkish; many are available via HathiTrust.

sources.name: Library of Congress — Islamic Manuscripts from Mali
sources.notes: Over 30 digitized manuscripts from Timbuktu collections; rights must be checked per item.

sources.name: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library — Islamic Manuscripts
sources.notes: Global Islamic manuscript holdings spanning multiple regions; discovery/digitization service, not blanket reuse authorization.

sources.name: DREAMSEA
sources.notes: Digital repository project covering Islamic and Buddhist manuscripts across Indonesia, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam.

sources.name: DREAMSEA Manuscripts Catalog
sources.notes: Searchable DREAMSEA catalog; individual records can expose IIIF manifests, languages, subjects and page counts.

sources.name: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin Digital Collections
sources.notes: SBB documents digitized Arabic/Yemeni and Islamic manuscript holdings; use item-level terms for release decisions.

sources.name: Islamic Scientific Manuscripts Initiative (ISMI)
sources.notes: Specialized discovery and metadata for Islamic scientific manuscripts in multiple languages.

sources.name: British Library Archives and Manuscripts Catalogue
sources.notes: Interim catalogue covering Oriental Manuscripts and Endangered Archives material; not all items are digitized or currently available.

sources.name: Malay World Manuscript Research Centre (PPMAM)
sources.notes: UKM research centre for Malay Jawi manuscripts; documents a worldwide research scope and manuscript holdings in libraries, archives and museums.

sources.name: UKM Learning and Research Repository — Manuscripts Collection
sources.notes: 78-item manuscript collection; catalogue includes religious works such as Tajwid, Hadith and Hanafi fiqh; file access varies by item.

sources.name: Osoul Global Center
sources.notes: Official Osoul site; multilingual dawah materials. Item-level license/redistribution terms must be verified before acquisition.

sources.name: Comprehensive Muslim e-Library (EDC)
sources.notes: EDC/Al-Najat library; free downloadable PDF catalog in many languages. Item-level rights must be verified before redistribution.

sources.name: Conveying Islamic Message Society (CIMS)
sources.notes: Egyptian non-profit society distributing Islamic books and pamphlets in multiple languages. Item-level rights must be verified.

sources.name: Zad Group
sources.notes: Saudi technology/media/publishing group with digital education and content services. No blanket open-license assumption.

sources.name: Mawthuq Islamic Content Archive
sources.notes: Provides JSON API access to content from multiple Islamic sites; API access is not itself redistribution permission.

sources.name: KFGQPC Developer Resources
sources.notes: Official King Fahd Complex developer/resource page. Specific datasets and translations require item-level rights verification.

sources.name: Islamic Content Association / IslamContent
sources.notes: Licensed Saudi association for multilingual Islamic content; official site states multilingual production and free electronic availability. Item-level terms still govern redistribution.

sources.name: Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies
sources.notes: Official Tafsir Center applications/resources, including Quran applications. API/data rights must be verified per resource.

sources.name: Alminasa.ai — المنصة الحديثية
sources.notes: Official platform for hadith research; official site and app materials describe interactive/semantic search, hadith-path visualization, narrator information, explanations and hadith grading tools. AI-assisted features are treated as research/indexing signals, not as independent scholarly evidence.

sources.name: Hdith.com — الموسوعة الحديثية
sources.notes: Digital hadith encyclopedia with structured hadith pages, isnad/narrator information, takhrij and scholar judgments visible on indexed pages. Content/licensing and bulk-access terms require item-level verification before redistribution.

sources.name: King Salman Complex for the Noble Prophetic Hadith
sources.notes: Official institutional source. Saudi regulations state the Complex serves hadith through collection, classification, verification, study and publication, including multilingual publication and use of modern technologies. Do not assume open/copy-left redistribution without explicit terms.

sources.name: Mubseroon — جمعية العوق البصري الأهلية ببريدة
sources.notes: Official Saudi association serving people with visual disabilities; its site documents Braille-related tools and a Braille learning platform. The stronger claims about a 45-language Islamic Open-API infrastructure were not independently verified, so they are not encoded as facts.

sources.name: HadithWeb — جامع خادم الحرمين الشريفين للسنة النبوية المطهرة
sources.notes: Officially documented hadith research program presented by the General Presidency for Scholarly Research and Ifta in cooperation with Harf Information Technology. The official description documents 33 core hadith books, 57 supporting works, hadith takhrij, narrator biographies exceeding 18,800 narrators, and other research services. Redistribution/API terms must be verified before acquisition.

sources.name: UmmahAPI
sources.notes: Public Islamic REST API covering Quran, hadith, tafsir, duas and other services. Official documentation states JSON REST endpoints and currently lists 36,000+ hadith from 10 collections and 12 Quran translations. API availability does not by itself grant redistribution rights for underlying source texts.

sources.name: Dua & Ruqyah — mrhrifat/dua-ruqyah
sources.notes: Public GitHub repository for a Dua/Ruqyah web app using Quran and hadith references, categories, translations and references. Repository is GPL-3.0, but the license applies to the code and does not automatically relicense third-party religious source data.

sources.name: Saudi Digital Library (SDL)
sources.notes: Candidate institutional academic-library source. Access, bulk acquisition, multilingual availability and redistribution rights must be verified per item/provider; no blanket public-domain claim is asserted.

sources.name: Islamic University of Madinah Digital Library
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific digital-library endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

sources.name: Umm Al-Qura University
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific library/repository endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

sources.name: Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific repository/library endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

notes: This expanded snapshot is not an exhaustive census of all global sources.
The 15 additions in this revision were checked against PR #541 and PR #558 diffs and the repository main-branch code search before insertion.

2026-09-24 verification: Alminasa.ai, Hdith.com, King Salman Hadith Complex, and Mubseroon were added as candidate sources after web verification. Claims about unrestricted/open licensing, exact corpus totals, or a KFUPM 'Hadith Cloud Computing' infrastructure were not asserted without verifiable primary evidence.
